problems.title: Lemma16 uses a false intermediate exponential bound
problems.source_location: Official Lemma 16, Appendix B, p.23; arXiv v1 Lemma 15, pp.11–12.
claim: For \(\varepsilon>0,\alpha>1,a,b\in(0,1)\) with \(a^{1-\alpha}b^\alpha\le e^{\varepsilon(\alpha-1)}\), Lemma 16 bounds \[(1-a)^\alpha(1-e^{-\varepsilon(1+\ell)}b)^{1-\alpha}\le\exp(e^{-\varepsilon(1+\alpha\ell)}).\] Its proof first claims the stronger intermediate upper bound \(\exp((\alpha-1)e^{-\varepsilon(1+\ell)}b-\alpha a)\).
analysis: Take \(\alpha=2\), \(\varepsilon=\log2\), \(\ell=1\), \(a=1/200\) and \(b=1/10\); the coupling hypothesis holds at equality. The displayed product is \(39601/39000\), exceeding the claimed intermediate bound \(e^{3/200}\). Indeed \(e^{3/200}<200/197<39601/39000\), with the last comparison reducing to positive integer difference \(1397\). The lemma's final bound \(e^{1/8}\) remains valid; only the intermediate step is refuted.
result: The first inequality of the current proof is false under the lemma’s own hypotheses. The counterexample does not falsify the lemma’s final statement or establish a larger privacy budget. Replacing that proof step suffices at the level established by the existing conditional derivation.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Keep the lemma’s domain and constants. Set \(p=\alpha/(\alpha-1)\), \(\lambda=e^{-\varepsilon(1+\alpha\ell)}\), and \(z=be^{\varepsilon\ell(\alpha-1)}\); the hypothesis gives \(a\ge\lambda z^p\). If \(z\ge1\), the original product is at most \(1\). If \(0<z<1\), its logarithm is at most \(L(\lambda)\), where \(L(s)=\alpha\log(1-sz^p)-(\alpha-1)\log(1-sz)\). To show \(L'(s)\le1\), multiply by the positive denominator: its numerator is \[H(s)=1-(\alpha-1+s)z+(\alpha-s)z^p+(s^2-s)z^{p+1}.\] On \([0,\lambda]\), \(H'(s)\le0\), so \(H(s)\ge H(1)=1-\alpha z+(\alpha-1)z^p\ge0\) by convexity. Integrating from \(L(0)=0\) gives \(L(\lambda)\le\lambda\), the original bound. This restores the lemma with unchanged constants; it is not an author-adopted erratum or an independent audit of every privacy proof.
